label: D2 after a2 led commonly to S2 (a2->S2 common transition), when value is high
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO), and almost only when the agent chose a2 and the shown state is S2 (common a2 transition): the bare predicate D2 & a2 & S2 has recall 0.997 and mass recall 0.999, but precision 0.62. Nothing fires on a1, on S1, or on rare transitions. The non-firing a2->S2 cases come late in the episode (rate drops after about trial 70, zero from trial 90 on; adding ep_trial < 80 gives F1 0.87) and at low model value. Restricting to value > 7.6 (the models own value output, which is observable to it) gives dev F1 0.88, mass recall 0.98. Magnitude rises with value: 74% of activation mass is in the top value bin (>8.1). All variables are observed at D2; no future variables used.

issues: The main claims hold on the test split. phase != D2 gets recall 0. D2 & common==0 gets recall 0.003. D2 & action==1 gets recall 0.002. D2 & a2 & S2 gets recall 0.997, precision 0.60, mass recall 0.999. D2 & a2 & S2 & ep_trial>=90 gets recall 0, so 'zero from trial 90' is right.

The value > 7.6 condition stands partly for episode position. Adding ep_trial<80 or <90 on top of value>7.6 changes nothing (F1 stays 0.878), and no step with ep_trial>=80 has value>7.6. Value is not purely a proxy, though. In early trials (ep_trial<60) the feature never fires when value<=7.6 (precision 0 over 2195 steps). The label's 'when value is high' is therefore fair.

One small systematic false-positive class: on the first a2->S2 trial after switching from a1 (prev_action==1), precision is only 0.19 over 5038 predicted steps. Excluding these raises test F1 from 0.878 to 0.891 (dev 0.896). The predicate when good==1 (S2 not the good state) is also weaker, with precision 0.56 vs 0.91 when good==2. That is hidden-state modulation, not a different trigger.
The remaining misses are mostly weak activations: the bottom activation quartile has coverage 0.65, and the misses hold only 2.2% of activation mass. This is scattered noise.
